PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : Ultra-sensitive Digital Quantification of Proteins and mRNA in Single Cells
Source Link  : https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-019-11531-z
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-019-11531-z
Journal      : Nature Communications, 2019, Vol. 10, Article 3544
Platform     : Automated microfluidic digital proximity ligation assay (u-dPLA); two-layer
               push-up PDMS device; ddPCR and one-step RT-ddPCR readout (Bio-Rad QX200)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes an automated microfluidic system for ultrasensitive, simultaneous
quantification of protein copy numbers and mRNA in individual mammalian cells, called
microfluidic digital proximity ligation assay (u-dPLA). The device traps and lyses single
cells in 7-nL nanoliter chambers, dramatically reducing the dilution factor relative to
regular well-plate dPLA. All assay steps are executed automatically with nanoliter precision
using Matlab-controlled pneumatic valve actuation, reducing pipetting errors to <0.1% versus
~10% for manual pipetting.

Key innovations over regular dPLA:
  - Up to 55-fold improvement in limit of detection (LOD)
  - 25-fold improvement in detection efficiency
  - 100% of single-cell sample used in ddPCR readout (vs 9% in regular dPLA)
  - Linear dynamic range of 3-4 orders of magnitude
  - Integrated live-cell time-lapse microscopy and chemical stimulation in the same device
  - Simultaneous protein and mRNA quantification via duplex one-step RT-ddPCR

The protocol is divided into three functional assay branches:
  1. Single-cell protein quantification via u-dPLA + ddPCR (FAM channel)
  2. Simultaneous protein/mRNA quantification via duplex u-dPLA + RT-ddPCR (FAM + VIC)
  3. HSV-1 viral infection heterogeneity: live-cell ICP4-YFP imaging + viral protein
     quantification by u-dPLA in the same single cells


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Two-layer push-up PDMS device bonded to glass slide (127.76 mm x 85.48 mm x 1 mm).
Chip capacity: 144 parallel single-cell dPLA assay units.

Fluidic layer (thick, top):
  - AZ40XT photoresist 18 um (rounded channels for valve sealing)
  - SU-8 22 um (medium feature channels)
  - SU-8 70 um two-layer (large reagent channels)

Control layer (thin, bottom):
  - SU-8 22 um; microfluidic push-up valves (Unger et al. Science 2000)
  - Pneumatically actuated via Matlab-controlled solenoid valves

Chamber architecture per assay unit (Chambers I-V):
  Chamber I   : Reagent input and wash channel; reagents introduced via dead-end filling
  Chamber II  : Single-cell trap (50 um constriction); cell imaged here and then lysed
  Chamber III : 7-nL lysis chamber; cell contents lysed and retained here; probe mixing zone
  Chamber IV  : Probe-lysate diffusion mixing extension; valve between III and IV opens
                during 1-h incubation to allow mixing by diffusion
  Chamber V   : Ligation reaction chamber; PLA products generated here
  Output port : 1930 um inner diameter biopsy punch; 9 uL PLA products retrieved per unit

Valve system:
  - Microfluidic valves separate each chamber to prevent contamination between steps
  - Dead-end filling delivers precise reagent volumes to empty chambers
  - Wash channels (MilliQ water) flush channels between reagent steps
  - Chip automation via Matlab program controlling valve open/close sequences


CELL LINES
----------
- HEK293T (human embryonic kidney): model cell for CD147/TNFR1 protein quantification
  and mRNA-protein correlation studies. TNFR1 not detected; consistent with no TNF-a
  response in NF-kB stimulation experiment.
  Cultured in DMEM (Cat. No. 11965-092, Life Technologies) + 10% FBS (F9665, Sigma-Aldrich).

- H1299 (human lung epithelial, NSCLC): primary cell line for TNFR1 protein/mRNA
  co-quantification and Spearman mRNA-protein correlation analysis.
  Cultured in RPMI-1640 (Cat. No. 11835-030, Life Technologies) + 10% FBS.

- A549 (human lung epithelial, adenocarcinoma): used for HSV-1 infection heterogeneity
  assay combined with live-cell ICP4-YFP imaging and viral protein u-dPLA.
  Cultured in DMEM (Cat. No. 86012804, Sigma-Aldrich) + 10% FBS.

All cells dissociated with TrypLE (Cat. No. 12605028, Life Technologies) 5 min at 37C,
resuspended in sterile PBS, filtered through 40 um cell strainer, diluted to 2x10^5
cells/mL for on-chip loading at 5 psi input pressure.


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | BSA Surface Blocking
  Reagents    : 10% BSA in PBS (Cat. No. 37525, Thermo Fisher)
  Duration    : 1 h (60 min)
  Temperature : 25C (room temperature)
  Purpose     : Coat PDMS chip surfaces to minimise non-specific adsorption of PLA probes
                and cell-lysate proteins to channel walls.
  Post-block  : Wash with MilliQ water; ventilate with compressed air before cell loading.

Step 2 | On-Chip Calibration Curve
  Reagents    : Purified protein standard (TNFR1, CD147, or CSTB), PBS, PLA Probes,
                Ligation Mix, MilliQ water
  Method      : Serial dilution of pure protein standards loaded into assay chambers via
                dead-end filling from lowest to highest concentration. 8 min wash between
                each concentration via Channel I.
  PLA probes  : 500 pM stock diluted to 2 nM in probe binding buffer (0.1% BSA +
                0.05% Tween-20 + 100 nM goat IgG + 0.1 g/L sheared salmon sperm DNA in PBS).
                Channel I flushed 2 min; Channel II flushed 15 min.
  Probe incub : 37C, 60 min (diffusion mixing)
  Ligation    : On ice 30 min; 37C 10 min; 65C 5 min (heat inactivation of T4 ligase)
  Retrieval   : 9 uL per unit, collected for ddPCR
  Purpose     : Calibration converts ddPCR amplicon counts per uL to absolute protein
                copy numbers. Run in parallel with single-cell experiments on the same chip.
  LOD calc    : 3 SD above background reading or y-intercept of fitted linear curve
                (whichever is higher).

Step 3 | Single-Cell Loading and Hydrodynamic Trapping
  Reagents    : SingleCell suspension in PBS, PBS
  Operation   : Pressure-driven flow-through trapping in Chamber II (50 um constriction)
  Loading     : 5 psi input pressure; 2x10^5 cells/mL
  Occupancy   : ~90% average single-cell occupancy per chip run
  Verification: Cell loading confirmed visually under microscope before proceeding
  Note        : Chip immediately moved to ice after loading confirmed.
                BioScript mix abstraction represents pressure-driven hydrodynamic trapping;
                no DMF electrode actuation is involved.

Step 4 | Single-Cell Lysis
  Reagents    : Lysis buffer (0.3x TM buffer + protease inhibitor in cell resuspension buffer)
  Operation   : Lysis buffer introduced from Chamber I to push and lyse cell from
                Chamber II into Chamber III (7 nL)
  Duration    : 10 min on ice (0C)
  Verification: Lysis confirmed visually under microscope
  Key feature : 100% of 7-nL single-cell lysate retained in Chamber III; zero sample loss.
                Regular dPLA loses 91% of sample (only 9% reaches ddPCR readout).
                This 11-fold increase in effective sample use is the primary driver of the
                55-fold LOD improvement.

Step 5 | PLA Probe Incubation with Cell Lysate
  Reagents    : PLA Probes (2 nM working concentration)
  Chambers    : III and IV (valve between open during incubation)
  Duration    : 60 min at 37C; diffusion-based mixing
  Mechanism   : Each PLA probe pair consists of two oligonucleotide-tagged antibodies
                recognising two distinct epitopes on the target protein. When both probes
                bind the same protein molecule, their oligonucleotides are brought within
                ~3-5 nm, enabling connector-mediated ligation.
  Probes used :
    TNFR1 : Biotinylated BAF225 (R&D Systems), streptavidin-biotin conjugation
    CD147 : Biotinylated BAF972 (R&D Systems), streptavidin-biotin conjugation
    CSTB  : Commercially available (Cat. No. 4405465, Applied Biosystems)
    HSV-1 : Anti-HSV-1 polyclonal ab9533 (Abcam), in-house DBCO-NHS/azide click chemistry;
             detects ~80 HSV-1 viral protein species encoded by HSV-1 genome

Step 6 | Ligation Reaction
  Reagents    : Ligation Mix (89.1 uL MilliQ water + 10 uL 10x ligase buffer +
                0.4 uL 1/500-diluted T4 ligase (EL0011, Thermo Scientific) +
                0.5 uL 1 uM connector oligo TTTCGACACGACACGATTTAGGTC per 100 uL)
  Operation   : Ligation mix pushes probe-lysate mix from Chambers III/IV into Chamber V
  On ice      : 30 min for diffusion mixing
  Ligation    : 37C, 10 min; T4 DNA ligase seals nick in connector-bridged probe pair
  Inactivation: 65C, 5 min; heat inactivation of T4 ligase
  Product     : Circular dsDNA PLA product; each molecule = 1 detected protein

Step 7 | PLA Product Retrieval and ddPCR (Protein Quantification Gate)
  Reagents    : MilliQ water (flush), ddPCR Supermix for Probes (Bio-Rad Cat. No. 1863024),
                Universal PCR Assay (Cat. No. 4405501, Applied Biosystems),
                Droplet Generation Oil (Cat. No. 1863005, Bio-Rad)
  Retrieval   : 9 uL PLA products flushed from Chamber V via water through 1930 um port
  ddPCR setup : 9 uL products + 10 uL 2x Supermix + 1 uL 20x PCR Assay = 20 uL total;
                loaded into DG8 cartridge with 65 uL Droplet Generation Oil (QX200, Bio-Rad)
  PCR program : 95C 10 min; 40x (94C 30s / 60C 1 min); 98C 10 min; ramp 1.5C/s
  Readout     : FAM channel; positive droplet count = absolute protein copy number
  ddPCR primers:
    Forward   : GCATCGTCTCGTGGGCTC
    Reverse   : TTGTACGCATGTGGACTTTAGACACGACACGA
  Detection   : ddPCRProteinDetection module; 30 s
  QC gate     :
    Pass (BB2): proteinSignal > 0 -> above LOD; dispose ddPCR droplets
    Fail (BB3): proteinSignal <= 0 -> below LOD; drain
  Results (selected):
    CD147 mean: HEK293T 197,785 (N=266); H1299 327,609 (N=96); A549 179,513 (N=98)
    TNFR1 mean: H1299 14,807 (N=88, range 6,310-33,541); A549 13,017 (N=84)
    TNFR1 in HEK293T: all below LOD (2,277 molecules); consistent with no NF-kB response
    Cells above TNFR1 LOD: 86% (149/174); first single-cell TNFR1 counts reported

Step 8 | Duplex Protein/mRNA Quantification (Same Single Cell)
  Reagents    : RNaseOUT (Cat. No. 10777019, Invitrogen; 20x dilution in all reagent mixes),
                One-step RT-ddPCR Supermix (5 uL), Reverse Transcriptase (2 uL),
                DTT 300 mM (Cat. No. 1864021, Bio-Rad; 1 uL),
                Universal PCR Assay 20x (1 uL),
                TNFR1 TaqMan Probe 20x (Cat. No. Hs01042313_m1, Applied Biosystems; 1 uL),
                Nuclease-free water (1 uL); Total: 20 uL
  Method      : PLA product retrieval (9 uL) includes protected mRNA; RNaseOUT added to all
                reagent mixes throughout chip steps to protect mRNA integrity
  Duplex      : FAM channel -> protein (PLA ligation products, same as Step 7)
                VIC channel -> mRNA (RT-ddPCR amplicons from TNFR1 mRNA)
  RT program  : 42C 1 h; 95C 10 min; 40x (95C 30s / 60C 1 min); 98C 10 min; ramp 2C/s
  Crosstalk   : VIC/FAM crosstalk negligible (Supplementary Fig. 5a/b)
  Detection   : rtDdPCRmRNADetection module (VIC channel); 30 s
  QC gate     :
    Pass (BB5): mrnaSignal > 0 -> mRNA detected; dispose duplex droplets
    Fail (BB6): mrnaSignal <= 0 -> mRNA below detection; drain
  Results     :
    Spearman rho (TNFR1 protein vs mRNA, H1299): 0.45 (N=38 single cells)
    Previous estimates: ~0.1 (Taniguchi 2010, Albayrak 2016, Darmanis 2016)
    Finding: Including lowly-expressing cells (previously below dPLA LOD) increases
    mRNA-protein correlation significantly. Spearman coefficient rises as low-protein
    cells are included in the calculation (Fig. 3e). High-sensitivity quantification is
    essential for accurate mRNA-protein correlation estimates.

Step 9 | HSV-1 Viral Infection Heterogeneity Assay
  Reagents    : HSV1_InfectedCell (A549 + HSV-1 ICP4-YFP, MOI 2, overnight), ControlCell
                (A549, no virus), PBS, LysisBuffer, PLAProbes (HSV-1), LigationMix,
                MilliQWater, ddPCR_Supermix, UniversalPCRAssay, DropletGenerationOil
  Cell prep   : HSV-1 stock prepared by Vero cell infection (MOI 0.01), harvested Day 3
                by three freeze-thaw cycles; stock concentration by plaque assay.
                A549 infected with 25 uL virus in 2 mL fresh medium overnight (MOI 2).
  Live imaging:
    Reporter  : ICP4-YFP; ICP4 expressed immediately upon viral genome nuclear entry,
                prior to genome replication (DeLuca et al. 1985; 1987).
                Nuclear YFP signal = infection proceeded to nuclear entry (YFP-positive).
    Modality  : Time-lapse fluorescence imaging on chip before lysis (liveCellImagingDetection)
    Calculation: Matlab imfindcircles locates cells; ImageJ Rolling Ball Background
                 Subtraction; total fluorescence = sum of all YFP pixel values within cell
  Lysis       : All cells lysed simultaneously with 0.3x TM buffer, on ice, 10 min
  HSV-1 PLA   : Polyclonal anti-HSV-1 ab9533 (Abcam) conjugated via DBCO-NHS click chemistry;
                detects ~80 viral protein species; both immediate-early, early, and late proteins
  Probe incub : 37C, 60 min
  Ligation    : On ice 30 min; 37C 10 min; 65C 5 min
  ddPCR       : Same protocol as Step 7; FAM channel; viral protein copy number per cell
  Detection   : viralProteinDetection module; 30 s
  QC gate     :
    Pass (BB8): infectionSignal > 0 -> ICP4-YFP+ (nuclear entry confirmed); dispose
    Fail (BB9): infectionSignal <= 0 -> uninfected or control (no YFP); drain
  Results     :
    N infected (YFP+) cells: 27; N control cells: 19
    Group difference p-value: 5.356e-11 (two-sided Welch's t test)
    Spearman rho (ICP4-YFP fluorescence vs total viral protein count): 0.48
    Interpretation: Not all YFP-positive cells progress past immediate-early protein
    synthesis stage; partial correlation (rho=0.48) indicates a sub-population undergoes
    abortive infection. Single-cell viral protein counts span ~5-fold range across
    infected cells, consistent with prior reports of substantial single-cell heterogeneity
    in viral progeny release (Heldt 2015, Russell 2018).


PERFORMANCE SUMMARY
-------------------
Protein target    LOD (on-chip)   LOD (regular)   Det. eff (on-chip)  Det. eff (regular)
TNFR1             2,277 molecules 66,789 molecules 33 proteins/DNA     741 proteins/DNA
CD147             2,795 molecules 55,385 molecules 29 proteins/DNA     70 proteins/DNA
CSTB              18,824 molecules 1,035,991 mol.  304 proteins/DNA    5,024 proteins/DNA

LOD improvement: up to 55-fold  |  Detection efficiency improvement: up to 25-fold
Dynamic range  : 3-4 orders of magnitude
Sample recovery: 100% of 7-nL lysate used (vs 9% in regular dPLA)
Chip capacity  : 144 parallel single-cell assay units


BIOSCRIPT COMPILER NOTES
-------------------------
BioScript file   : lin2019_udpla_single_cell_protein_mrna.bs
Compiler         : lilott8/BioScript (ANTLR4-based)
IR output        : 10 basic blocks (BB1-BB10), 3 if/else gates, 12 CFG edges
DAG file         : lin2019_udpla_single_cell_protein_mrna_main_dag.dot
Duration units   : All durations in s (seconds) or m (minutes); BioScript h token unsupported
Duration notes   :
  60 min probe incubation / RT step -> 60m -> IR: 3600.0 SECOND
  30 min ligation on ice            -> 30m -> IR: 1800.0 SECOND
  10 min lysis / ligation at 37C   -> 10m -> IR: 600.0 SECOND
  40 PCR cycles x 90s each         -> 60m -> IR: 3600.0 SECOND (modelled as one heat block)
Modules          : ddPCRProteinDetection, rtDdPCRmRNADetection,
                   liveCellImagingDetection, viralProteinDetection
Manifests        : PBS, LysisBuffer, PLAProbes, LigationMix, MilliQWater,
                   BSA_BlockingBuffer, SingleCell, PurifiedProteinStandard,
                   RNaseOUT, RTddPCR_Supermix, ReversTranscriptase, DTT,
                   UniversalPCRAssay, TaqMan_TNFR1_Probe, ddPCR_Supermix,
                   DropletGenerationOil, HFE7500_Surfactant,
                   HSV1_InfectedCell, ControlCell
Mix abstraction  : `mix X with Y for T` abstracts valve-gated dead-end filling and
                   diffusion-based mixing inside sealed nanoliter chambers; no DMF electrode
                   actuation involved; fluid movement is pneumatically driven via
                   Matlab-controlled valve sequencing.
Heat abstraction : `heat` abstracts both on-chip incubation (0C ice, 37C, 65C) and
                   off-chip ddPCR thermal cycling (95C, 94C, 98C) in the QX200 instrument.
Detect abstraction: `detect` abstracts ddPCR/RT-ddPCR positive-droplet counting (FAM/VIC
                   channel readouts) performed off-chip after product retrieval.
ASCII compliance : All Unicode characters replaced with ASCII equivalents for ANTLR4
                   FileStream compatibility (u for micrometer/microliter; rho for Spearman
                   correlation symbol). Verified: 0 non-ASCII bytes.

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidic 5-Plex Fluorometric Enzyme Assay for Newborn Screening of Pompe, Fabry, Hunter, Gaucher, and Hurler Lysosomal Storage Diseases from a Single Dried Blood Spot Punch

REAGENTS USED:
  - DBS Extract (single 3-mm dried-blood-spot punch eluted in 100 uL of 0.1% w/v Tween20 extraction buffer, 30 min on an orbital shaker at ambient temperature; one extract shared across all 5 assays)
  - GAA Reagent (Pompe assay: 4-methylumbelliferyl-alpha-D-glucoside substrate with acarbose inhibitor and 20.0 mmol/L methyl-beta-cyclodextrin)
  - GLA Reagent (Fabry assay: 4-methylumbelliferyl-alpha-D-galactoside substrate with N-acetyl-D-galactosamine inhibitor and 20.0 mmol/L methyl-beta-cyclodextrin)
  - IDS Reagent (Hunter assay: 4-methylumbelliferyl-alpha-L-iduronate-2-sulfate substrate with 20.0 mmol/L methyl-beta-cyclodextrin)
  - GBA Reagent (Gaucher assay: 16 mmol/L 4-methylumbelliferyl-beta-D-glucoside substrate with 1.5% sodium taurocholate, no inhibitor)
  - IDU Reagent (Hurler assay: 2 mmol/L 4-methylumbelliferyl-alpha-L-iduronide substrate with 3.0 mmol/L D-saccharic acid 1,4-lactone inhibitor and 20 mmol/L methyl-beta-cyclodextrin)
  - Extraction Buffer (EXT: 0.1% w/v Tween20 in water)
  - Stop Buffer (STB: 0.2 mol/L NaHCO3, pH 10.0, 0.01% w/v Tween20)
  - Calibrant (4-methylumbelliferone, 4-MU, standard used for a 4-point calibration curve run in duplicate)

STEPS:
1. Four-point fluorescence calibration (in duplicate): dispense triple-sized calibrant droplets from each of 4 calibrant reservoirs and read fluorescence for each, giving 8 calibration readings used to build a linear-regression calibration curve.
2. Substrate/reagent background: for 2 of the 44 sample positions, use extraction buffer alone (no DBS extract) merged with each of the 5 reagents, incubate under the same conditions as sample reactions, and read background fluorescence for each of the 5 assays.
3. For each of the remaining DBS extracts loaded onto the cartridge (up to 42 additional samples): dispense one extract droplet and merge it separately with each of the 5 reagents (GAA, GLA, IDS, GBA, IDU) to form 5 parallel reaction droplets from the single punch.
4. Incubate all 5 reaction droplets per sample at 37 C for 1 h.
5. Stop and read: merge each incubated reaction droplet with its corresponding stop buffer droplet and measure endpoint fluorescence for each of the 5 assays (excitation 370 nm / emission 460 nm), converting readings to enzymatic activity via the calibration curve after subtracting background.
6. Screening interpretation: compare each of the 5 endpoint activities against the normal/affected separation boundary established from presumed-normal and confirmed-affected samples; flag and discard reaction droplets whose activity falls at or below the cutoff as presumptively affected (Pompe, Fabry, Hunter, Gaucher, or Hurler), otherwise report as normal.

gba_bg_reagent = dispense 1 units of gba_reagent

        dispose gba_final

    dispose gla_final
    dispose ids_final

  - No-Template Control (no DNA)

STEPS:
1. For each of the four allelic controls (allele 1 only, allele 2 only, both alleles, no template), dispense a ~300 nL droplet of the control template onto the electrowetting chip.
2. Dispense a matching ~300 nL droplet of TaqMan master mix reagent for each control.
3. Actuate and merge each control droplet with its corresponding master mix droplet on the electrowetting chip to form four complete PCR reaction droplets.
4. Transport each droplet back and forth several hundred times under electrowetting control to verify standard droplet manipulations (transport, mixing, splitting, dispensing) are unaffected by the PCR reagents, then position the droplets at opposite ends of the electrode array.
5. Remove the electrowetting control voltage and thermocycle the entire chip inside the custom-built hot-air thermocycler mounted on the fluorescence microscope.
6. After each thermal cycle, read out FAM and VIC fluorescence intensity from each droplet in real time to build per-cycle amplification time-courses.
7. Discard each droplet after the thermocycling/detection run is complete.

ASSAY TYPE: Droplet-Based PCR Thermal Cycling on a Microelectrofluidic System (MEFS)

REAGENTS USED:
  - DNA Sample (target genomic DNA solution containing the region to be amplified)
  - PCR Reagent (primer pair, all four deoxyribonucleoside triphosphates (dNTPs), and a heat-stable Taq DNA polymerase)

1. Dispense a DNA sample droplet and a PCR reagent droplet (primers, dNTPs, Taq polymerase).
2. Merge the sample and reagent droplets to form the PCR master-mix droplet.

   a. Strand separation: heat to 95C for 45 seconds to separate the parent DNA duplex strands.
   b. Hybridization of primers: cool to 54C for 30 seconds to allow each primer to anneal to its complementary strand.
   c. DNA synthesis: heat to 72C for 90 seconds, the optimal temperature for Taq DNA polymerase, to extend and synthesize new DNA strands from each primer.
4. After thermal cycling completes, detect the fluorescence signal from the amplified DNA droplet.
5. Discard the analyzed droplet.

  - Extraction Buffer (DPBS supplemented with 0.1% v/v Tetronic 90R4)[cite: 58]

  - DMF-Compatible Wash Buffer (DPBS supplemented with 0.1% v/v Tetronic 90R4)[cite: 58]
  - Conjugate Solution (HRP-conjugated anti-human IgG)[cite: 58]
  - Luminol Enhancer Solution (SuperSignal ELISA Femto chemiluminescent component)[cite: 58]
  - Stable Hydrogen Peroxide (H2O2) Solution (SuperSignal ELISA Femto chemiluminescent component)[cite: 58]

STEPS:
1-4. On-Chip Blood-Plasma Separation: Dispense a five-unit extraction-buffer droplet (~6.5 uL) onto the extraction zone, and dab whole blood (~55 uL) onto the plasma separation membrane (SM) where cells are trapped while filtered plasma wicks through the transport membrane (TM) for ~3 min; drive the extraction droplet through the TM (~30 s) to extract and collect the filtered plasma into a droplet.
5. Particle Dispensing: Dispense a double-unit droplet of virus-coated paramagnetic particles into the assay zone and immobilize using the magnetic lens while moving supernatant to waste.
6. Plasma Capture: Actuate the separated plasma droplet to the assay zone, deliver it to the paramagnetic particles, actively mix for 7 min, immobilize particles, and move supernatant to waste.
7-12. Initial Wash Cycle: Dispense a double-unit droplet of wash buffer, deliver to the particles, actively mix for 30 s, immobilize particles, and move supernatant to waste; repeat this wash step a total of 6 times.
13. Conjugate Addition: Dispense a double-unit droplet of HRP-conjugated anti-human IgG conjugate solution, deliver to the particles, and actively mix for 5 min.
14-17. Post-Conjugate Wash: Repeat the wash cycle (dispense wash buffer, mix for 30 s, immobilize, move supernatant to waste) a total of 4 times.
18. Final Pre-Detection Wash: Dispense a double-unit droplet of wash buffer, mix for 10 s, actuate the droplet to the detection zone, immobilize particles, and move supernatant to waste.
19. Substrate Addition (Luminol): Dispense a single-unit droplet of luminol enhancer solution, deliver to the paramagnetic particles, and actively mix for 10 s.
20. Substrate Addition (H2O2): Dispense a single-unit droplet of stable H2O2 solution, deliver to the droplet containing particles, and actively mix for 80 s to initiate the chemiluminescent reaction.
21. Detection & Readout: Measure the resulting chemiluminescence for 120 s (collecting data at 60 Hz and recording the mean of the final 40 seconds) using the integrated photomultiplier tube (PMT).

PROTOCOL DESCRIPTION
====================

Title        : A Microfluidics Approach Towards High-Throughput Pathogen Removal from Blood Using Margination
Source Link  : https://pubs.aip.org/aip/bmf/article/6/2/024115/923894
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1063/1.4710992
Journal      : Biomicrofluidics, 2012, Vol. 6, Article 024115
Platform     : Pressure-driven continuous-flow PDMS microfluidic device; cascaded straight margination channels with bifurcation outlets


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a label-free, high-throughput microfluidic blood filtration technique for
non-specific removal of blood-borne pathogens and inflammatory cellular components from whole blood,
inspired by the in vivo microcirculatory phenomenon of leukocyte margination. The device exploits
the Fahreaus effect: as whole blood flows through narrow 20x20 um microchannels, deformable red
blood cells (RBCs) migrate axially to the channel centre under Poiseuille flow, forming an RBC-rich
core and a cell-free layer adjacent to the channel walls. Mechanical collisions between migrating
RBCs and other cellular components (bacteria, yeast, platelets, and leukocytes) drive their radial
displacement into the cell-free wall region -- a phenomenon termed margination.

At the downstream bifurcation (1:8:1 ratio), marginated cells are skimmed off via narrow side
channels (waste) while RBC-enriched, pathogen-depleted blood exits the large centre outlet. Two
margination channels are cascaded in series: the bacteria-depleted blood from stage 1 enters stage 2
with higher hematocrit, amplifying Fahreaus effect and RBC-bacteria hydrodynamic interactions, and
achieving overall bacterial removal efficiency greater than 80% in a single pass.

The technique requires no sample preparation, no magnetic labelling, and no sheath flow. Whole blood
can be drawn directly from patients and pumped into the device, making it suitable for a blood
dialysis circuit concept for adjunctive sepsis treatment.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Fabrication : PDMS (Sylgard 184, Dow Corning); standard soft lithography; silicon master patterned
              by deep reactive ion etching (DRIE); PDMS 10:1 prepolymer:curing agent, cured 70 C
              for 2 h; bonded to glass slides by air plasma (Harrick Plasma Cleaner); left 2 h at
              70 C to complete bonding; 1.5 mm holes punched for inlets and outlets.
Silanization: Trichloro(1H,1H,2H,2H-perfluorooctyl)silane 1 h (silicon wafer and PDMS master).

Single-channel device:
  - First margination channel : 20 um (W) x 20 um (H) x 5 mm (L); aspect ratio = 1
  - Second margination channel: 20 um (W) x 20 um (H) x 1 mm (L); aspect ratio = 1
  - Bifurcations in series    : 1:8:1 (side:centre:side outlet ratio)
  - Expanded bifurcation      : channel expands to 200 um width to enhance cell-free layer
  - Side outlet width         : 20 um (skims leukocytes 8-15 um; flow ratio 1:4 side:centre)
  - Throughput                : 1 mL/h per channel at 15 uL/min

Parallel 6-channel device:
  - 6 cascaded-design channels in parallel with additional upstream filter region
  - Filter region removes clogs and debris before margination channels
  - Throughput: 6 mL/h (100 uL/min total); performance equivalent to single-channel device

Flow driver  : Syringe pump (NE-1000, New Era Pump Systems Inc.)
Imaging      : Olympus IX71 inverted phase contrast microscope + Hamamatsu C4742-80-12AG CCD;
               IPLAB software (video acquisition); ImageJ (analysis)
Confocal     : LSM 510 meta laser scanning confocal (Carl Zeiss) on Axiovert 100 M Inverted;
               488 nm excitation; 10x objective + 2.5x digital zoom; 1 um z-interval; 512x512 px


SEPARATION PRINCIPLE
--------------------
Aspect ratio : Low aspect ratio (height/width <= 1; 20x20 um square channels) gives isotropic
               shear distribution across the channel cross-section, closely resembling circular
               blood vessels. RBC axial migration distances are equal in all directions, forming
               a well-defined RBC core and enabling efficient margination to all four sidewalls.
               High aspect ratio channels (>1) produce blunt z-direction velocity profiles and
               uneven margination, trapping bacteria at the mid-plane.

Flow rate    : Bacteria margination efficiency increases with flow rate and plateaus above
               10 uL/min. At high flow rates (Re ~4-5), RBCs experience higher shear and
               inertia, accelerating axial migration and RBC-bacteria interactions. Inertial
               focusing is negligible in whole blood at Re << 50.

Cascaded design: Removing plasma and marginated bacteria at stage 1 bifurcation increases
               hematocrit of blood entering stage 2 (~10% increase). Higher hematocrit enhances
               platelet and bacteria diffusivity at the RBC core periphery and increases frequency
               of RBC-bacteria collisions, driving further margination in stage 2.

Yeast vs bacteria: S. cerevisiae (~5 um ovoid; elastic modulus ~1e8 Pa) is larger and stiffer
               than E. coli (~2x0.5 um rod; ~1e7 Pa). Larger size drives stronger margination
               towards all four channel corners, yielding higher removal (~90%) than bacteria (~80%).
               Rod-shaped bacteria also undergo additional tumbling/rotational motion that enhances
               lateral drift across streamlines.


CELL LINES AND PATHOGENS
-------------------------
E. coli      : Strain HB101 K-12; GFP-expressing (arabinose-inducible); cultured overnight at
               37 C in LB Agar + ampicillin 100 ug/mL + arabinose 0.1%; harvested and
               resuspended in 1x PBS before use. Spiked at 1e6-1e7 CFU/mL.
               For device characterisation: Alexa Fluor 488 E. coli K-12 BioParticles
               conjugates (Invitrogen) used for FACS analysis.

S. cerevisiae: Haploid W303-1B strain; YFP-expressing; gift from Dr. Jacquin Niles, MIT
               Department of Biological Engineering. Spiked at 1e6-1e7 per mL.
               Morphology (~5-7 um ovoid) representative of pathogenic Candida albicans.

Human blood  : Whole blood (Research Blood Components, Brighton MA).
               Device characterisation: washed 3x with PBS + 0.5% BSA; resuspended at 45%
               hematocrit in PBS + 0.5% BSA + 3% w/v Dextran-40.
               Whole-blood pathogen removal experiments: fresh unwashed blood used directly.


PROTOCOL STEPS
--------------

Step 1 | RBC Sample Preparation (Device Characterisation)
  Reagents    : Whole blood, PBS + 0.5% v/v BSA (wash buffer),
                PBS + 0.5% v/v BSA + 3% w/v Dextran-40 (sample buffer)
  Operation   : Wash RBCs 3x with wash buffer (centrifuge 300 x g, 5 min each wash).
                Resuspend at 45% hematocrit in sample buffer.
  BioScript   : Centrifugation abstracted as heat at 25c (no centrifuge primitive).
                Each wash cycle: mix 5m + heat at 25c for 5m.
  Notes       : Dextran-40 prevents RBC sedimentation during syringe pump operation.
                For pathogen removal experiments using fresh whole blood, this step is skipped.

Step 2 | Antibody Staining for Cellular Analysis
  Reagents    : Fresh whole blood (unwashed), CD41a-FITC (1:50, BD Biosciences),
                CD45-APC (1:100, BD Biosciences)
  Operation   : Incubate blood with antibodies at 4 C for 40 min without prior washing.
  Purpose     : CD41a-FITC labels platelets; CD45-APC labels leukocytes.
                Staining in fresh blood preserves native cell populations for FACS analysis.

Step 3 | Microbial Spiking
  Reagents    : GFP-E. coli (resuspended in 1x PBS), YFP-S. cerevisiae
  Operation   : Add each microbe to antibody-stained blood at 1e6-1e7 per mL; vortex 30 s.
  Notes       : Both microbe types spiked simultaneously for combined whole-blood analysis.
                Separate experiments performed for E. coli vs S. cerevisiae to quantify
                removal efficiency by CFU counting and haemocytometer independently.

Step 4 | Stage 1 Margination (First Channel, 5 mm)
  Input       : Spiked whole blood loaded at inlet via syringe pump
  Flow rate   : 15 uL/min (Re ~4-5; wall shear rate ~6e4 s-1)
  Operation   : Continuous laminar flow through 20x20 um channel (5 mm). RBCs migrate
                axially to form RBC-rich core; bacteria, yeast, platelets, and leukocytes
                marginate to cell-free wall region via RBC mechanical collisions.
  Bifurcation : 1:8:1; channel expands to 200 um at bifurcation to enhance cell-free layer.
                Marginated cells collected in narrow side channels (20 um; drain/waste).
                RBC-enriched, pathogen-depleted blood exits large centre outlet (ratio 8).
  Stage 1 result: ~50% bacterial removal; hematocrit increases ~10% in centre outlet.
  BioScript   : mix abstracts laminar co-flow through margination channel;
                rbcSuspension supplies RBC hydrodynamic environment.

Step 5 | Stage 2 Margination (Cascaded Channel, 1 mm)
  Input       : Stage-1 filtered blood (higher hematocrit, reduced bacteria)
  Flow rate   : 15 uL/min (continuous from stage 1)
  Operation   : Bacteria-depleted blood undergoes second round of margination. Higher
                post-stage-1 hematocrit amplifies Fahreaus effect and RBC-bacteria
                collision frequency; additional bacteria driven to channel periphery.
  Bifurcation : 1:8:1; second waste stream drained; final filtered blood collected.
  Stage 2 result: cumulative >80% bacterial removal, >80% platelet and leukocyte depletion,
                ~90% S. cerevisiae removal, ~30% increase in RBC concentration at centre outlet.
  Haemolysis  : Negligible (optical absorption 414 nm); RBC transit time < 0.01 s in
                high-shear margination zone.

Step 6 | FACS Analysis of Filtered Blood
  Instrument  : BD LSR II flow cytometer (BD Biosciences)
  Gating      : FSC/SSC + fluorescence: CD41a-FITC (platelets), CD45-APC (leukocytes),
                GFP (E. coli), YFP (S. cerevisiae)
  Normalisation: Concentration at centre outlet / inlet sample concentration (%)
  QC gate     : cellularComponentDetection module; 30 s detect
                Pass (separationSignal > 0): >80% removal confirmed; dispose filtered blood
                Fail (separationSignal <= 0): insufficient removal; drain; re-optimise

Step 7 | Bacterial CFU Quantification
  Operation   : Plate 10 uL aliquots from inlet and centre outlet on LB agar.
                Incubate 24 h at 37 C. Count colony-forming units (CFUs).
  Removal efficiency = 1 - (CFU_outlet / CFU_inlet)
  Yeast count : Haemocytometer (independent of FACS/CFU pipeline).
  BioScript   : 24 h incubation = 1440 min (compiler duration constraint; IR: 86400.0 SECOND)
  QC gate     : bacterialColonyCount module; 30 s detect
                Pass (bacteriaSignal > 0): >80% bacterial removal confirmed; dispose
                Fail (bacteriaSignal <= 0): insufficient removal; drain; flag for re-run

Step 8 | Parallel Device Validation (6-Channel Scale-Up)
  Device      : 6 cascaded-design channels in parallel + upstream filter region
  Flow rate   : 100 uL/min total (6 ml/h)
  Result      : Similar platelet, leukocyte, and bacteria filtration performance to single channel
  Note        : Further parallelisation (100+ channels) or device stacking could approach
                conventional dialysis throughput (~1-2 L/h)

BIOLOGICAL CONTEXT: THE NF-kB SIGNALING NETWORK
-------------------------------------------------
NF-kB family transcription factors (RelA/p65, RelB, c-Rel, p50, p52) are activated by
dozens of signals from pathogens and host tissue. The dominant dimer in most cell types
is p65/p50. Prior to stimulation, NF-kB dimers are sequestered in the cytoplasm by
inhibitor of kappa B (IkB) proteins (IkBa, IkBb, IkBe, IkBg, IkBd/p100).

Canonical activation: ligand -> receptor -> ubiquitination/kinase cascade ->
IKK complex activation (IKKa, IKKb, NEMO) -> IkB phosphorylation and degradation ->
NF-kB nuclear translocation -> target gene transcription.

Key negative feedback loops:
  - IkBa (fast; newly translated IkBa exports NF-kB from nucleus; re-synthesised every
    cycle; responsible for oscillatory dynamics)
  - A20 (upstream of IKK; edits ubiquitin scaffolds on TRAF complexes; induced by
    nuclear NF-kB; establishes ~60 min refractory state)
  - CYLD (deubiquitinates IKK scaffolds; upstream of IKK)
  - IRAK-M and MyD88S (TLR/IL-1R pathway specific; induced by nuclear NF-kB)
  - IkBd/p100 homodimer (noncanonical; broad cross-tolerance on 24 h timescale)

Oscillatory dynamics: Under continuous TNF-a, NF-kB undergoes damped oscillations with
~90 min period in fibroblasts. IKK cycling between neutral (n), active (a), and inactive
(i) states is required for sustained translocation cycles. These oscillations are
stimulus-specific: TNF-a drives oscillations in macrophages, fibroblasts, and epithelial
cells, while LPS drives singular (non-oscillatory) activation in fibroblasts.

IMPORTANT BIOLOGICAL FINDINGS ENCODED IN THIS PROTOCOL
-------------------------------------------------------
1. Pulsatile stimulation reveals hidden network properties:
   Comparing pulsatile vs. continuous TNF-a stimulation revealed that IKK cycling
   between active and inactive states is essential for NF-kB signal transduction
   (Behar & Hoffmann Biophys. J. 2013; Ashall et al. Science 2009).

2. NF-kB acts as a differentiator for TNF-a and IL-1b:
   NF-kB responds to CHANGES in cytokine concentration (delta), not absolute levels.
   This enables spatial interpretation: the network infers relative distance to
   cytokine-secreting sentinel cells from the rate of cytokine concentration change.
   PAM2CSK4 does NOT exhibit this behavior - selective processing of stimulus dynamics.
   (Son et al. Sci. Signal. 2021 - ref 13)

3. Sequential stimulation encodes memory via ligand-specific feedback:
   IRAK1 autophosphorylation creates cross-tolerance between IL-1b and LPS but not
   TNF-a, reflecting receptor pathway topology (shared vs. distinct myddosome use).
   4-ligand sequences produce unique NF-kB oscillation pattern fingerprints.
   (Wang et al. Cell Rep. 2022 - ref 15; DeFelice et al. Sci. Signal. 2019 - ref 64)

4. NF-kB dynamics determine downstream gene expression:
   Different oscillation properties (amplitude, duration, period) produce distinct
   transcriptional outputs in single cells. Stable NF-kB oscillation at fixed period
   increases downstream gene expression.
   (Kellogg & Tay Cell 2015 - ref 17; Lane et al. Cells 2017 - ref 120)

5. Limitation of endpoint measurements:
   Single time-point cytokine measurements (e.g. serum TNF-a in sepsis) show low
   correlation with disease severity. Increasing/decreasing cytokine dynamics are
   far better predictors (e.g. IL-6 kinetics in septic shock mortality).
   Microfluidic dynamic stimulation is required to capture true in vivo signal
   processing. (Abasiyanik et al. Nat. Commun. 2020 - ref 115)

OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol introduces NIMS (Nanostructure-Initiator Mass Spectrometry), a matrix-free
surface-based mass spectrometry technique for spatially defined, high-sensitivity analysis
of biomolecules, metabolites, and drugs directly from cells, tissues, and biofluids.

The NIMS surface is a porous silicon chip (~10 nm pores, fabricated by anodic etching)
loaded with perfluorinated siloxane initiator molecules that are trapped inside the pores
in a clathrate-like ordered arrangement. Laser or ion irradiation rapidly vaporises the
initiator, triggering desorption and ionisation of analytes adsorbed on the surface --
without any conventional MALDI matrix. This eliminates matrix-related background, crystal
size limitations on spatial resolution, and the need for sample preparation steps.

Key advantages over existing techniques:
  - No matrix required (vs MALDI); no background below m/z 700
  - Lateral resolution ~150 nm with ion-NIMS Bi3+ beam (vs >10 um matrix crystal for MALDI)
  - Reduced molecular fragmentation vs secondary-ion mass spectrometry (SIMS)
  - Direct analysis of sub-microlitre blood and urine without extraction or derivatisation
  - Multiply charged protein ions analogous to ESI (laser-NIMS)
  - Compatible with laser (N2, 337 nm) and multiple ion sources (Au+, Ga+, Bi+, Bi3+)

  PROTOCOL: FUCOSYLTRANSFERASE INHIBITION ASSAY USING IMAGE-ANALYSIS
             AND DIGITAL MICROFLUIDICS (DMF)
================================================================================

  Source Link : https://www.shihmicrolab.ca/_files/ugd/f0a828_fb291b4dee6147cd9c47c11d6308710c.pdf
  Paper DOI   : https://doi.org/10.1063/1.5088517
  Journal     : Biomicrofluidics 13, 034106 (2019)

================================================================================
  OVERVIEW
================================================================================

This protocol describes a fluorescence-based inhibition assay for
H. pylori alpha(1,3)-fucosyltransferase (FucT) performed on a digital
microfluidic (DMF) device. The assay uses the labeled synthetic disaccharide
4-methylumbelliferyl beta-N-acetyllactosaminide (MU-beta-LacNAc) as a
substrate. When FucT is active, it fucosylates MU-beta-LacNAc, preventing
its hydrolysis by glycoside hydrolases and resulting in low fluorescence.
When FucT is inhibited (e.g., by GDP), the substrate remains unfucosylated,
gets cleaved by BgaA and SpHex, and releases fluorescent 4-methylumbelliferone
(4-MU). Inhibition curves spanning four orders of magnitude are generated
on-device via serial dilution, with concentrations verified by an image-based
"pixel count" method.

================================================================================
  PLATFORM & DEVICE SPECIFICATIONS
================================================================================

  Platform        : Two-plate digital microfluidic (DMF) chip
  Chip dimensions : 3 x 2 in. (75 x 50 mm)
  Electrodes      : 93 actuation electrodes (avg. width ~1 mm) +
                    10 reservoir electrodes (4.1 x 3 mm^2 each) +
                    1 waste collection electrode
                    Total: 103 electrodes
  Electrode shape : "Skewed-wave" (sinusoidal intercalating, ~4.0 x 0.87 mm^2)
                    Minimum angles ~90 deg to prevent dielectric breakdown
  Electrode gap   : 30 um (interelectrode average)
  Plate gap       : ~140 um (two layers of double-sided tape)
  Top plate       : ITO-coated glass (Rs = 15-25 ohm)
  Bottom plate    : Chromium electrode-bearing glass with FluoroPel PFC1601V
                    hydrophobic coating
  Driving voltage : 120-160 VRMS at 15 kHz
  Automation      : Arduino Uno + PCB relay board + PaseMaker software
                    (Python 2.7, LLGUI.exe interface)
                    GitHub: https://github.com/shihmicrolab/Automation
  Imaging         : 3.0 MP CMOS USB camera (EO-3112C, Edmund Optics) +
                    10x C-mount close focus zoom lens (54363, Edmund Optics)

     - Use: diluent for serial dilutions and blank control

     - 0.08 mM GDP-fucose
     - 25 mM HEPES pH 7.0, 0.05% Pluronics F-68

     - 10 mM MgCl2

     - 0.02 mM GDP-fucose

================================================================================
  ASSAY PRINCIPLE
================================================================================

  UNINHIBITED (low/no GDP):
    MU-beta-LacNAc --[FucT + GDP-fucose]--> Fucosylated-MU-beta-LacNAc
    Fucosylated substrate is NOT cleaved by BgaA/SpHex --> LOW fluorescence

  INHIBITED (high GDP):
    GDP competes with GDP-fucose at FucT active site --> FucT blocked
    MU-beta-LacNAc remains unfucosylated
    Unfucosylated MU-beta-LacNAc --[BgaA then SpHex]--> 4-MU (fluorescent)
    --> HIGH fluorescence

  Fluorescence readout: lambda_ex = 365 nm, lambda_em = 460 nm

================================================================================
  ON-DEVICE PROTOCOL (42-STEP DMF PROCEDURE)
================================================================================

------------------------------------------------------------------------
  STEP 1 — Prime HEPES Buffer Reservoirs
------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - Manually pipette five droplets (~2.7 uL each) of 25 mM HEPES buffer
    onto five separate reservoirs on the DMF chip.
  - Place the ITO top plate on top of the device.
  - Apply silicone oil shell to each droplet using an oil-coated pipette tip.
  - These reservoirs serve as diluents for the serial dilution (Steps 3-10).

------------------------------------------------------------------------
  STEP 2 — Load GDP Inhibitor Stock
------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - Pipette a ~3.1 uL droplet of 80 mM GDP solution to one of the five
    pipetting inlet electrodes (aligned to the edge of the ITO).
  - Apply a driving potential to the inlet electrode to pull the droplet
    under the ITO into the reservoir gap.
  - Apply silicone oil shell.
  - This minimizes time on-chip before use, reducing biofouling risk.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
  STEPS 3-10 — Serial ~5.5-Fold Dilution of GDP (6 Concentrations)

Title        : Membrane-less Microfiltration Using Inertial Microfluidics
Source Link  : https://www.nature.com/articles/srep11018
Paper DOI    : https://doi.org/10.1038/srep11018
Journal      : Scientific Reports, 2015, Vol. 5, Article 11018
Platform     : Multiplexed inertial microfluidics (spiral PDMS microchannels, trapezoidal
               cross-section, passive pressure-driven flow; no external force fields)


OVERVIEW
--------
This protocol describes a membrane-less microfiltration system based on massively parallelised
inertial microfluidics, capable of processing macroscopic sample volumes at ~500 mL/min. The
device consists of multiple PDMS layers with embossed spiral microchannels of trapezoidal
cross-section (~200 individual spirals in a full multiplexed unit). Individual separation
channels share a common inlet and exit through two outlets; cells subjected to hydrodynamic
inertial lift and Dean drag forces migrate to size-dependent equilibrium positions and are
collected at either the inner or outer outlet.

The protocol is divided into three independent applications demonstrated in the paper:
  1. CHO / Hybridoma cell retention from perfusion bioreactors (filtration mode, ~500 mL/min)
  2. Yeast (S. cerevisiae) microfiltration for broth fermentation clarification (~320 mL/min)
  3. CHO-K1 cell cycle synchronisation by size-based fractionation (150-300 mL/min)

As cells are separated solely by hydrodynamic forces from externally-driven flow, the system
runs continuously without membrane replacement, eliminating the major operating cost driver of
conventional microfiltration systems.


DEVICE ARCHITECTURE
-------------------
Material     : Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS), Sylgard 184 (Dow Corning), 10:1 base:curing agent.
               Baked at 70 C for 2 h; final bonded assembly baked at 70 C for 2 days.
Fabrication  : Soft lithography; SolidWorks master mold design; precision micro-milling on
               aluminium (Whits Technologies, Singapore); PDMS layers bonded by O2 plasma
               (Harrick Plasma, USA) with manual alignment.
Fluid delivery: 3D-printed SLA guide layer with internal fluidic channels and conical pins;
               distributes flow equally across all microchannels.

CHO / Hybridoma filtration and fractionation device:
  - Cross-section : Trapezoidal, 600 um wide x 80x130 um
  - Loops         : 8; radius 8-24 mm
  - Spirals/layer : 4 (connected internally)
  - Multiplexed   : 84 spirals → 500 mL/min combined (~350 L/Day single unit)

Yeast filtration device:
  - Cross-section : Trapezoidal, 450 um wide x 30x70 um
  - Spirals/layer : 8
  - Multiplexed   : 180 spirals → ~320 mL/min combined

Inlets  : 1 shared inlet per multiplexed unit (sample loaded via peristaltic pump)
Outlets : 2 per unit
  - Outer outlet : Cell concentrate / recycle (filtration) or small-cell fraction (fractionation)
  - Inner outlet : Clarified filtrate / product harvest (filtration) or large-cell fraction


WORKING PRINCIPLE
-----------------
Inertial lift force (F_L proportional to a_p^4): arises from the balance of shear-induced
and wall-induced lift forces in straight channels; drives particles toward channel wall
equilibrium positions.

Dean drag force (F_D proportional to a_p^2): generated by two counter-rotating Dean vortices
in the top and bottom halves of curvilinear channels; applies drag transverse to the main
flow direction.

The trapezoidal cross-section creates stronger Dean vortex cores near the outer wall,
enhancing separation throughput and efficiency compared to rectangular channels.

Filtration mode  (~6 mL/min per spiral): inertial lift forces dominate; all particles focus
near the outer wall and exit via the outer outlet (cell concentrate). Cell-free medium exits
via inner outlet.

Fractionation mode (~1.5-2 mL/min per spiral): size-differential equilibrium positions emerge;
small cells (<14 um, G0/G1) remain trapped in Dean vortices near outer wall; large cells
(>14 um, G2/M) focus near inner wall. Each population exits a different outlet.


CELL LINES
----------
- AE-1 Hybridoma (ATCC HB-72): IgG1-secreting; model for perfusion bioreactor CHO retention
  and productivity monitoring. Cultured in Hybridoma-SFM (Gibco) at 100 rpm, 37 C, 5% CO2.
- CHO-K1 (ATCC CCL-61): adherent Chinese Hamster Ovary cell line; used for cell cycle
  synchronisation. Cultured in low-glucose DMEM + 10% FBS + 1% pen/strep, 37 C, 5% CO2.
- Saccharomyces cerevisiae (Sigma-Aldrich, dry strain): model small microorganism (3-5 um);
  used to demonstrate yeast broth clarification and benchmark vs commercial membrane filters.

APPLICATION 1: CHO / Hybridoma Cell Retention from Perfusion Bioreactor

  Purpose   : Wets PDMS microchannels; eliminates air bubbles. BSA (0.5%) and EDTA (2 mM)
